entities.name: Alonso de Fonseca y Ulloa
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alonso de Fonseca y Ulloa (died 1473) was a powerful Roman Catholic prelate whose ecclesiastical career and political maneuvering significantly shaped the turbulent landscape of 15th-century Castile during the waning years of the Trastámara dynasty. Serving successively as Bishop of Ávila (1445–1454), Archbishop of Seville (1454–1464), and Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela (1465–1469), Fonseca strategically consolidated vast spiritual and temporal influence across the Iberian Peninsula. His lineage, the noble Fonseca family, was instrumental in forging alliances and power bases that would prove crucial in the dynastic struggles preceding the reign of the Catholic Monarchs.

Fonseca's ascent was marked by a series of shrewd political appointments and exchanges, often leveraging his family's standing and considerable wealth. As Archbishop of Seville, he played a central role in the Castilian Civil War (1465–1469), initially supporting Henry IV against the rebellious faction that favored Alfonso, Prince of Asturias. However, his allegiances shifted with the political winds, as he later became a prominent figure in the league of nobles who challenged Henry's authority. His most notable maneuver involved a controversial exchange of archiepiscopal sees with his nephew, Alonso de Fonseca y Acevedo, in 1465, allowing him to gain control over the wealthy and strategically important Archdiocese of Santiago de Compostela in Galicia, a move that highlighted the pervasive nepotism and political bartering within the Castilian Church.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alonso de Fonseca y Ulloa was a pivotal figure in 15th-century Castilian politics and church administration, whose strategic maneuvering and accumulation of power significantly influenced the transition period leading to the reign of the Catholic Monarchs. His actions consolidated regional ecclesiastical power and demonstrated the profound intertwining of spiritual and temporal authority.
